issues.description: The DMA-stream accessor and I/O methods replace the original public `&self` interface with methods that require callers to supply an internal `RwLockReadGuard`, changing the public API/behavior instead of keeping synchronization behind the object boundary.
issues.rationale: The reviewed revision makes `daddr`, `direction`, `paddr`, `reader`, and `writer` public associated functions over `RwLockReadGuard` rather than methods over `&DmaStream`. Callers must now acquire/pass the implementation's internal guard, and the original object-level API is no longer preserved. Collaborator rikosellic explicitly warns that this modification changes behavior and explains that a bare `&RwArc` cannot support stable inner-value postconditions across concurrency. The author clarifies the intended two-layer solution: a public `f(&RwArc)`/`&self` wrapper acquires the lock and delegates to a verified guard method; the reviewer says that splitting approach is acceptable. The next relevant commit, `4b848d3f...`, implements exactly that resolution by renaming the guard methods to private `*_inner` functions and adding public `&self` glue wrappers that acquire `read_inner()`.

219-221: pub fn direction(this: &RwLockReadGuard<...>) -> DmaDirection

Fix evidence in commit 4b848d3f: these functions become private `*_inner`; public `daddr(&self)`, `direction(&self)`, `paddr(&self)`, `reader(&self)`, and `writer(&self)` acquire `self.read_inner()` and delegate.
issues.verification: Source and Git-history adjudication; historical Verus not executed locally. Verified the selected historical head and true merge-base, confirmed all five guard-only public APIs in ff234245, inspected the direct child 4b848d3f, and confirmed that it both privatizes/renames the guard-level functions and restores public `&self` wrappers. The final head retains that two-layer design and has successful build and format-and-verify checks.
